title: Shared workload
text: A teammate is overloaded while others wait for assignments.

options.label: Rebalance together
options.now: You agree a fairer task split.
options.success: The new split reduces missed handovers.
options.failure: Uneven experience leaves gaps in the new split.

options.label: Take the difficult tasks
options.success: The backlog clears, but the team still relies on you.
options.failure: Your own workload becomes the next bottleneck.

options.label: Keep current targets
options.success: The team catches up without a new rota.

title: Whose idea?
text: A colleague says their idea was presented without credit.

options.label: Correct the record
options.success: Shared credit brings the colleague back into planning.
options.failure: The correction helps trust, but the dispute still slows work.

options.label: Arrange a private talk
options.now: You hear both accounts before reporting back.
options.success: A clear agreement settles future credit.
options.failure: Without a public correction, the complaint persists.

options.label: Focus on the result
options.success: The project proceeds, though trust remains strained.
options.failure: The colleague stops sharing useful suggestions.

title: First delegation
text: A teammate wants to lead a task they have not handled before.

options.label: Delegate with checkpoints
options.now: You agree two checkpoints and a clear handover.
options.success: The colleague completes the task with useful feedback.
options.failure: A checkpoint catches mistakes, but delivery needs rework.

options.label: Let them own it
options.now: They get the whole task and its responsibility.
options.success: They develop confidence and deliver independently.
options.failure: A missed warning turns into a late handover.

options.label: Keep it yourself
options.now: You keep control of the task.
options.success: Delivery is sound, but the colleague gains no experience.
options.failure: Your crowded schedule delays the task.

title: An unusual fault
text: A colleague brings a problem the standard checklist cannot explain.

options.label: Trace the cause together
options.now: You compare evidence before changing the work.
options.success: You identify the underlying fault and document it.
options.failure: The evidence rules out several causes, but the fault remains.

options.label: Try a controlled change
options.now: You isolate one variable and record the result.
options.success: The controlled change reveals a useful fix.
options.failure: The change fails and needs to be reversed.

options.label: Use the usual workaround
options.success: The workaround holds under normal demand.
options.failure: The hidden fault returns under pressure.

title: Quality at speed
text: A colleague asks which checks can be shortened for a deadline.

options.label: Keep the critical checks
options.now: You protect key checks and trim low-risk repetition.
options.success: The work passes review without a preventable defect.
options.failure: The important checks hold, but the deadline slips.

options.label: Ask for more time
options.now: You explain the evidence behind an extension.
options.success: The extra time produces a stronger handover.
options.failure: The extension is refused; the work needs a smaller scope.

options.label: Use a small sample
options.now: You note the reduced sample in the handover.
options.success: The sample catches the main issue this time.
options.failure: A missed defect needs a costly internal correction.

title: Teach the method
text: A colleague wants to learn a difficult part of your work.

options.label: Guide a practice attempt
options.now: You demonstrate, then let them try with feedback.
options.success: The colleague can use the method without constant help.

options.label: Write a short guide
options.now: You record the steps and the common failure signs.
options.success: The guide improves repeat work and handovers.
options.failure: The guide misses a situation that needs judgment.

options.label: Demonstrate once
options.success: They pick up the essentials from the demonstration.
